name: 75 Hard
tagline: Mental toughness program: diet, two workouts, water, reading, daily photo.
description: Created by Andy Frisella, 75 Hard is framed as a mental toughness program rather than a fitness plan. You commit to five non-negotiable tasks every single day for 75 consecutive days. There are no cheat days, no modifications, and no substitutions — missing any task on any day means starting over from Day 1.
strictModeDisclaimer: The original 75 Hard rule is: miss a single task on a single day and you restart from Day 1. Turning this on means Vectis will ask you to confirm each day and will reset your progress if you report a miss. Leave it off to track the challenge without the restart penalty.

tasks.title: Follow your diet (no cheat meals, no alcohol)

name: 75 Soft
tagline: A more flexible version of 75 Hard, with a weekly rest day.
description: 75 Soft keeps the spirit of 75 Hard — building daily discipline over a 75-day stretch — but relaxes the rules so it's more sustainable. Alcohol is allowed on social occasions, one rest day per week is built in, and there's no restart-on-miss rule, making it a gentler entry point into structured daily challenges.

tasks.title: Eat healthy (alcohol only on social occasions)

name: Whole30
description: A 30-day elimination diet designed to reset eating habits. You cut out added sugar, alcohol, grains, legumes, and dairy entirely for the full 30 days, then reintroduce food groups one at a time afterward to see how your body reacts.

tasks.title: No sugar, alcohol, grains, or dairy

name: Dry January
description: A month-long break from alcohol, traditionally done in January after the holiday season. The goal is simply consistency — no drinks for the full 31 days.

name: Couch to 5K
tagline: Structured run/walk plan building up to a 5K.
description: A gradual training plan that alternates walking and running in increasing intervals over roughly 8 weeks, designed to take a beginner from little to no running experience to comfortably completing a 5K.

name: 100 Days of Code
tagline: Code for at least an hour, every day.
description: A community coding challenge: commit to writing code for at least one hour a day for 100 consecutive days, tracking progress publicly to build a consistent habit.

name: The Miracle Morning
tagline: A structured early-morning routine, every day.
description: Based on Hal Elrod's book, this challenge is about starting each day with a deliberate routine before the day's demands take over — traditionally summarized as the SAVERS: Silence, Affirmations, Visualization, Exercise, Reading, and Scribing (journaling).

tasks.title: Morning routine (silence, affirmations, visualization, exercise, reading, scribing)

name: No-Spend Challenge
description: A month of spending only on essentials — rent, bills, groceries — while cutting out discretionary purchases entirely. Often used as a reset for spending habits or to jump-start savings.
